In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Al-Masad

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perished are the hands of Abu Lahab, and perished is he.﴾ At-tabb: cutting.

From the same root is batta (with the ba' placed before the ta'), which revolves around the meaning of cutting, as the science of linguistic roots (fiqh al-lughah) indicates in the revolving of a root around a single meaning.

And he said: at-tabb, at-tabab, at-tibab, at-tabib, and at-tatbib: deficiency and loss, up to his saying: "Tabbat yadahu" means: his two hands were lost and ruined.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: at-tabbat means destruction, and its parallel is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh is nothing but in ruin﴾ [Ghafir: 37], i.e., in destruction.

This is because Abu Lahab destroyed himself through his corrupt belief and his evil deeds. As came in the Sunnah, the saying of the Bedouin: "I am destroyed and I have destroyed," meaning: by his having intercourse with his wife in Ramadan. And there came His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So their gods, which they called upon besides Allah, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came; and they increased them in nothing but ruin﴾ [Hud: 101].

They said: "in nothing but loss," and loss leads to destruction and cutting off.

As came in its meaning in the story of Salih, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who would protect me from Allah if I disobeyed Him? You would only increase me in loss﴾ [Hud: 63]. From all of this it becomes clear that the meaning of "Perished are the hands of Abu Lahab" revolves between the meanings of cutting, destruction, and loss.

As for their being cut off: he was not able to have his hands cut off before his death.

As for destruction and loss: he was destroyed by the boil (ghuddah).

As for loss: how great was his loss after this judgment against him from Allah, may He be exalted.

(p-144) And since the meaning has been determined by the explicit text of the Qur'an as destruction and loss, what is the significance of attributing tabb to the two hands?

The answer: this is from the figure of speech of mentioning a part and intending the whole, as was previously mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿a lying, sinning forelock﴾ [Al-Alaq: 16], although the liar is its owner.

We have already stated there that this kind of style necessarily involves an increased specificity of the mentioned part to the intended meaning.

Since lying blackens the face and humbles the forelock, and its opposite, truth, whitens the face and honors the forelock, He attributed lying there to the forelock to increase its specific association with lying over the hand, for example.

And since destruction and loss are largely due to what the limbs earn, and the hand is most specifically associated with that, tabb was attributed to it.

What indicates that the one meant is the owner of the two hands is what follows it: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and perished is he﴾, i.e., Abu Lahab himself.

Whether His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Perished are the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ is informative or performative, it is possible from the standpoint of wording.

But His saying after it, ﴿and perished is he﴾, is informative, so the first would be performative, like His saying: ﴿Cursed is man, how ungrateful he is!﴾ [Abasa: 17].

Then the second came as confirmation of it. And the reading of Ibn Mas'ud was "wa-qad tabba" (and he has indeed perished).

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 111, verse 2:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿What his wealth availed him, nor what he earned﴾. Whether *ma* is interrogative, in which case it is an *istifham inkari* (a rhetorical question of denial), or negative, in which case it explicitly states that his wealth did not avail him anything.

And His saying: ﴿nor what he earned﴾.

It was said: that is, from his first wealth, what he inherited, or what he earned through deeds that brought upon him this ruin, namely his enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

A parallel to this verse is the earlier one: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into the pit]﴾ [al-Layl: 11].

The discussion of it has already preceded there.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already explained the meaning of ﴿What his wealth availed him, nor what he earned﴾ at His saying: ﴿Behind them is Hell, and what they earned will not avail them anything, nor what they took as protectors other than Allah; and for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10].

He also cited all the texts on this meaning in full.

**Note**

There are two questions regarding this verse:

First: The Prophet (ﷺ) was, while among his people in Makkah, gentle and forbearing. So how did he confront his uncle with this supplication: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾?

The answer is that he was gentle with them as long as he hoped for their Islam. When he despaired of that, this supplication was in its proper place. This is like what occurred from Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who was gentle with his father: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan﴾ [Maryam: 44], and ﴿O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a straight path﴾ [Maryam: 43]. When he despaired of him, he disassociated himself from him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was compassionate and forbearing﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114].

The second question concerns the coming of His saying ﴿and perished﴾ after ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, although the first clause is sufficient, whether it is an invocation against him or a report that this had occurred.

The answer, and Allah knows best, is this: the first clause could be understood as a report, and Allah erases what He wills and establishes. Or it could be an invocation that is not necessarily carried out, like His saying: ﴿Destroyed is man; how ungrateful he is﴾ [Abasa: 17]. Or it could be understood as censure and condemnation only. So ﴿and perished﴾ came to show that it will certainly befall him, and that he is among those against whom the word of your Lord has come into effect, so that the Prophet (ﷺ) would despair of his becoming Muslim, and the Muslims would despair of his becoming Muslim. Then the gentleness with him ends. Allah knows best.

What Allah reported has indeed occurred. It is among the miracles of the Qur'an that what it reported occurred exactly as it reported, and did not fail.

﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115], and His saying: ﴿Thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who defied, that they will not believe﴾ [Yunus: 33].

(p-146) We ask Allah for well-being; indeed He is All-Hearing, Responsive.
